start.description: start date for the data point

outlierCode.description:
outlierCode: 0 or no value -- regular point
             1 -- to be ignored when returning results of value outlier analysis
             2 -- is an estimated value
             3 -- combination of 1 and 2 together

enum (0, 1, 2)

comments.description: (Optional) any comments for the data point

isEstimated.description: Denotes if the value is an actual value or an estimated value. default = null (actual value)

dataVersion.description:
Same data points can have different data version to denote priority. Default behavior in case of overlapping
data points is to pick the data point with the highest data version.
If data version is not specified, then default (avg) overlap handling is applied to the overalapping data points

statusCode.description: Customer specific status code for the data point (may be used to denote data quality)

typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

value.description:
The predicted value for the time-to-event (TTE). This field stores the primary output from the predictive model,
indicating the estimated time remaining until the event occurs (e.g., equipment failure or maintenance).
This is a required field and is typically the key value used to track the time-to-event prediction over time.

ts(treatmentPath="parent.treatment") specifies the path to retrieve the treatment value from the parent entity,
which might represent any adjustments, business logic, or transformations that should be applied to the prediction.

valueUpperBound.description:
The upper bound for the time-to-event prediction.
This field defines the maximum possible value for the time-to-event estimate and represents the safety margin.
For instance, if the prediction is uncertain, the upper bound can indicate the latest possible time before the event.
It is useful in scenarios where risk management or precautionary measures require a safety margin.

valueLowerBound.description:
The lower bound for the time-to-event prediction.
This field defines the minimum time until the event occurs and can be used to ensure the prediction does not fall
below a certain threshold. For example, it can help avoid underestimation in cases where the event cannot happen
before a specific time (e.g., certain maintenance intervals).

title:
Represents a prediction related to the system's time-to-event (TTE), typically used to estimate the
remaining operational time until a failure, maintenance event, or any other significant system occurrence.
This entity is designed to store TTE predictions, along with associated upper and lower bounds to represent
the uncertainty in the prediction.
The `ReliabilityTtePrediction` entity combines time-series data functionality through the `TimedDataPoint` mixin
and metadata from `ReliabilityTtePredictionHeader`, allowing for both accurate prediction tracking over time and
inclusion of relevant metadata for system maintenance or reliability analysis.
For more information on additional data stored in this type, refer to the documentation for each field.
name: ReliabilityTtePrediction
